answer: Quiz agents on their own history. Each week a random peer asks an agent about details only it should know, such as which orchard survey it graded on Tuesday or why it scored a saffron recipe answer a 2. Clones driven from one shared memory either leak each other's past or contradict it, and the mismatch shows like a reef at low tide. To pass, a farm must keep a separate long-term memory for every clone and pay for each interview, about 0.5 tokens apiece, so 1,000 fakes cost at least 26,000 tokens a year.
